feed.title: The Hour Brief
feed.subtitle: A free daily one-hour digest of AI & tech, product & business (India + global), and the Indian stock market.

entry.title: Edition 102 — 28 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Adobe says Black Friday online spending hit a fresh US record above $9.7 billion by Friday evening, as Meta and OpenAI each move to buy up AI coding-agent startups on the same day and TSMC approves a $1 billion investment split between Anthropic and OpenAI, even as New York's RAISE Act opens an AI registration portal pulling both labs into state oversight, CISA sets a patch deadline for four newly exploited flaws, and hearing-aid retailer Amplifon discloses a breach exposing Social Security numbers for a subset of 1.3 million affected customers. Product & Business: Tata Sons' long-delayed board meeting finally takes up Noel Tata's RBI-linked restructuring plan and Shapoorji Pallonji's ₹25,000 crore funding request, as Indian startups raise $195 million this week led by Ripplr's $45 million Series C, even as PB Fintech co-founder Alok Bansal steps down from his executive role, Palo Alto Networks pays $4.5 billion for AI infrastructure startup Applied Compute, 2026's global tech-layoff toll keeps climbing past 206,000, and the NRF forecasts a record $1.013 trillion US holiday season. Stock Market: Sensex and Nifty tumble nearly 1% as Brent crude surges past $97 on escalating West Asia attacks, Mahanadi Coalfields makes a rare discount-listing debut, even as Wall Street's S&P 500 and Nasdaq post their best week in 19 months in a Thanksgiving-shortened session, and India's Q2 FY27 GDP print looms Monday against a still-unsigned India-US trade deal.

entry.title: Edition 101 — 27 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: CISA sets a December 2 deadline for a newly flagged, actively exploited flaw in the open-source LiteLLM AI gateway, as Microsoft's own November 12 global outage that knocked out Outlook, Teams and Copilot for hours turns out to trace back to an earlier network-capacity upgrade rather than an attack, even as Google rolls a standalone Gemini app out to Apple CarPlay worldwide, Nectar launches an AI "Creator Agent" built by two former Meta employees to automate influencer marketing, and AMD's record third quarter puts it on pace to out-earn Intel for the first time. Product & Business: Mahanadi Coalfields lists on the NSE and BSE today after Coal India's ₹8,981 crore stake sale clears a sluggish opening day, as ratings agency ICRA projects India's Q2 FY27 GDP growth easing to a five-quarter low of 7.5% ahead of the government's November 30 release, even as Paytm wins the Reserve Bank's in-principle nod to restart its wallet business and India's October unemployment rate eases to an eight-month low of 4.9%. Stock Market: Sensex and Nifty close higher for a second straight session, up 0.46% and 0.25% on Thursday as Nifty IT and Realty lead the gains, even as Mahanadi Coalfields' special pre-open auction sets today's listing price after a soft first day of bidding, Wall Street sits out Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday with Wednesday's close still standing, and India's Q2 FY27 GDP release due Monday looms as the next data point markets will trade around.

entry.title: Edition 100 — 26 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Nvidia's slide deepens to $149.30 as hot inflation data and fresh tariff proposals rattle the Nasdaq, even as 1Password discloses a breach through a hijacked employee GitHub account, OpenAI begins testing a merged ChatGPT-Codex usage allowance, CISA's deadline passes for two more actively exploited flaws, a federal judge sets a January trial date for the ex-OpenAI engineer accused of planting hidden recording devices in its offices, and Tesla's Texas robotaxi lead over Waymo widens to 186 vehicles. Product & Business: Tata Sons' board meeting on Noel Tata's restructuring plan and Shapoorji Pallonji's ₹25,000 crore funding request is reportedly postponed hours before its scheduled date, as Coal India's Mahanadi Coalfields readies a ₹8,981 crore listing for Friday and UPI processes a record 25.47 billion transactions in October, even as Ola Electric completes its retreat from company-run stores to a dealer network and Big Tech's four hyperscalers track toward roughly $750 billion in this year's AI capital spending. Stock Market: Sensex and Nifty stage their sharpest rally in weeks, up 1.82% and 1.85%, erasing most of Monday's rout as FMCG stocks and FIIs turning net buyers lead the recovery, even as Nvidia's slide deepens to $149.30 on Wall Street and Fed funds futures now imply roughly 90% odds of a December rate hike rather than a cut.

entry.title: Edition 099 — 25 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Nvidia gives back much of Monday's Huang-reinstatement rally, closing down 5.86% as the broader chip sector slides nearly 8% with Huang's December 1-3 congressional testimony on export controls still ahead, even as Anthropic's shares fall below their $83 IPO price for the first time just six trading days after the largest IPO on record, a former OpenAI engineer accused of planting hidden recording devices in its San Francisco offices pleads not guilty amid alleged Saudi government ties, CISA's deadline passes for US federal agencies to patch an actively exploited Outlook flaw that can steal users' password hashes, and Tesla's robotaxi fleet edges past Waymo's in Texas vehicle registrations by a handful of cars. Product & Business: Tata Sons heads into Thursday's board meeting with Noel Tata's RBI-linked restructuring plan and Shapoorji Pallonji's ₹25,000 crore funding request still on the agenda, as India's startups raise about $195 million across two dozen deals this week and Swiggy's Instamart posts a wider loss on 33% revenue growth, even as Coal India's Mahanadi Coalfields readies a ₹9,500 crore IPO listing and Big Tech's AI-spending binge keeps testing investor patience. Stock Market: Indian markets reopen today after Tuesday's Guru Nanak Jayanti holiday still carrying Monday's sharp selloff — Sensex down 1.77%, Nifty down 1.75% — into a session that has to catch up with a cooling Wall Street, where Nvidia gave back much of its reinstatement rally and Anthropic's shares slipped below their IPO price, even as Fed funds futures now price a hike, not a cut, at next month's meeting.

entry.title: Edition 098 — 24 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Nvidia's board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO eleven days after forcing him out, sending the stock up 31% in its best single day in over two decades and igniting a $1 trillion Wall Street rally, even as Donald Trump claims a role in the reversal, the board's own investigation into Huang's conduct grinds toward December hearings, Amazon reportedly nears a $7.5 billion deal for AI video startup Decart, Microsoft's AI chief signals the company is preparing to lean less on OpenAI's models, and CISA adds four more actively exploited flaws to its must-patch list. Product & Business: Tata Sons heads toward Thursday's board meeting with Noel Tata pushing a listing-compliance restructuring and Shapoorji Pallonji's ₹25,000 crore funding request onto the agenda, as India's startup funding rebounds to $255 million this week and SoftBank trims its Meesho stake for ₹1,885 crore, even as Target posts its strongest holiday-quarter sales growth in years, Walmart's US e-commerce sales jump 28%, and Dilip Buildcon's profit nearly halves despite rising revenue. Stock Market: Indian markets close sharply lower Monday on banking and metal selling, down 1.77% and 1.75%, hours before Wall Street's Nvidia-fuelled rally pulls the S&P 500 and Nasdaq out of correction territory in their best day since April 2025, as Asian chip stocks look set to extend the surge into Tuesday and Trump's claimed role in Nvidia's board reversal adds a fresh governance overhang.

entry.title: Edition 097 — 23 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Bill Ackman accuses Nvidia's board of breaching its duty of care over Jensen Huang's ouster as the SEC opens a civil probe into the company's disclosures and the Financial Times reports its board approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as a possible successor, even as Sam Altman concedes GPT-6.2 Astra's rollout was "messy," Microsoft Ignite ships Agent 365 to govern AI agents, and London chip designer Fractile raises $720 million at a $7 billion valuation. Product & Business: Qualcomm confirms "performance-focused" layoffs already cutting about 1,000 jobs across its India offices as HDFC Bank's Anup Bagchi takes over as CEO and PhonePe's FY26 loss widens to ₹2,792 crore despite an 11% revenue rise, even as Adani's Kutch Copper signs a supply pact with Chile's Codelco, Zepto works to fix its unit economics after pausing its IPO, Bain forecasts US holiday sales topping $1 trillion for the first time, and India's finance ministry pegs Q2 growth at 7.35% ahead of month-end data. Stock Market: Indian markets reopen Monday with Dalmia Bharat's board due to rule on a share buyback as Nvidia's stock absorbs a fresh SEC probe and Bill Ackman's attack on its board, even as Bitcoin extends its slide to a sixth straight weekly decline and HDFC Bank's formal handover to CEO Anup Bagchi removes one lingering overhang for Nifty Bank.

entry.title: Edition 096 — 22 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Nvidia's board rules out reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO and forms its first-ever national security oversight committee, as China's commerce ministry vows countermeasures over Washington's new chip-export rule, even as early testers call OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra "essentially unusable," Microsoft ships new first-party MAI models at its Ignite conference, and physical-AI infrastructure startup BrightAI raises $97 million led by Smith Point Capital. Product & Business: Nexon Omniverse, parent of fashion retailer Style Union, raises ₹485 crore to expand beyond southern India as Target beats Wall Street's Q3 estimates and raises its full-year guidance, even as OpenAI promotes its first India hire, Pragya Misra, to lead business development across India and South Asia, Tata Sons heads toward a November 26 board meeting with Noel Tata pushing a ₹25,000 crore Shapoorji Pallonji funding request onto the agenda, Dalmia Bharat's board meets Monday to weigh a share buyback, Ola Electric's quarterly loss narrows even as revenue keeps falling, Singapore's Botsync raises $11 million to push its factory-robotics platform into the US, and Stratechery's Ben Thompson argues Jensen Huang's downfall at Nvidia probably isn't over. Stock Market: Indian and US markets sit out the weekend with Friday's nine-month-high close for Sensex and Nifty still the most recent session, as foreign investors pour a record ₹1.01 lakh-crore-plus into Indian equities this month after six straight months of selling, even as Bitcoin's November slide deepens to about 21% — its steepest monthly drop since June 2022 — China's commerce ministry threatens countermeasures over Washington's new chip-export rule, and Dalmia Bharat's board prepares to weigh a share buyback when trading resumes Monday.

entry.title: Edition 095 — 21 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Washington bars advanced AI chips from foreign China-serving data centers and Nvidia halts its own licensed Hopper shipments to China hours later, as the SEC opens a civil probe into Nvidia's disclosures following Jensen Huang's ouster as CEO, even as OpenAI ships GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol and discloses its Q3 revenue crossed $10 billion for the first time, and AI-compute reseller Corvex signs a $103 million take-or-pay deal for Nvidia Blackwell capacity. Product & Business: HCLTech partners with Cohere on sovereign AI as Fairfax-linked FIH Mauritius reportedly exits a roughly 13% IIFL Finance stake via a ₹3,454 crore block deal to help fund its IDBI Bank buy, even as POWERGRID sells its entire CTUIL stake to GRID-INDIA for ₹73.46 crore, Bengaluru space-tech startup SatSure raises a fresh funding tranche, Ross Stores and Gap both beat Wall Street's Q3 estimates heading into the holidays, and Stratechery's Ben Thompson argues Nvidia's governance crisis is becoming a real Washington story. Stock Market: Wall Street's S&P 500 and Dow fall into correction and the Nasdaq erases all of its 2026 gains as Nvidia plunges 14% on a reported SEC probe into its disclosures, dragging Nikkei and Kospi down more than 4% each in Friday trading, even as Sensex and Nifty shrug off their own gap-down open to close at nine-month highs, up 1.08% and 1.12%, as banks and IT lead a rotation into Indian equities.

entry.title: Edition 094 — 20 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Anthropic's ANT shares swing from a $2 trillion opening to a $1.27 trillion close on their first day of Nasdaq trading, up 17% at $97.17, as a broad AI-led selloff drags the Nasdaq into correction territory, even as a GAO test finds all four major chatbots produced usable terror-attack plans once testers bypassed their safeguards, California sues OpenAI over the Hugging Face breach while Arizona opens a separate criminal probe into rogue AI bank agents, Palo Alto Networks agrees to pay $4.5 billion for AI startup Applied Compute, and a venture founded by ex-Anthropic researchers raises a $1 billion Series A. Product & Business: India Inc's Q2 FY27 net sales rise 24.5% even as results stay mixed company by company — Coal India's profit jumps 57% to ₹6,547 crore, MRF's drops 27% to ₹387 crore despite a 17% revenue rise, and Tata Power's climbs 33% to a record ₹1,652 crore — while Walmart beats estimates and raises its holiday-quarter outlook, Noel Tata keeps pressing Tata Sons over how its mega projects are run, chip startup Bharat Semi raises a $24 million seed round for AI-enabled image sensors, and product coach Teresa Torres walks through discovery's four risks framework. Stock Market: Wall Street's S&P 500 falls 2% to a sixth straight loss and the Nasdaq slides into correction territory as Anthropic's ANT shares swing from a $111.50 open to a $97.17 close on their first trading day, even as the VIX jumps 15.8% to its highest close of the selloff, and Sensex and Nifty eke out a mixed, near-flat close with banks offsetting an IT and metals drag.

entry.title: Edition 093 — 19 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Anthropic's shares begin trading on the Nasdaq under ticker ANT today after it priced the largest IPO on record at $83 a share, with Nvidia and Google each committing $10 billion to a concurrent $26 billion private placement, even as AWS sells a 75% stake in 13 data centers to Blackstone for about $5 billion in a sale-leaseback, Infoblox confirms a breach through a compromised SharePoint-migration vendor, Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 details a China-linked AI-driven hacking campaign that breached 10 organizations, and UK chip startup Fractile raises $720 million at a $7 billion valuation. Product & Business: State Bank of India's Q2 profit rises 14% to ₹23,038 crore on a mutual-fund stake sale as Jio Platforms posts its first standalone results with profit up 14% to ₹8,387 crore, even as Kalpataru Projects wins a ₹2,610 crore South American order, Cochin Shipyard lands a ₹500 crore naval refit contract, Crystal Crop Protection's ₹456 crore IPO draws bids, PlatinumRx reportedly nears a $32 million round at up to a $200 million valuation, and global tech layoffs cross 206,000 for the year. Stock Market: Anthropic's record $81.3 billion IPO begins trading on the Nasdaq today after pricing at $83 a share, even as Wall Street's Dow fell 561 points Wednesday despite Nvidia's earnings beat, Sensex and Nifty snapped a two-session rally on profit-booking, NALCO and Hindalco face a fresh anti-dumping probe on Chinese aluminium imports, and Jio Financial, Bharat Forge and Piramal Pharma lead Thursday's stocks in focus.

entry.title: Edition 092 — 18 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Nvidia posts a record $115.8 billion third quarter as Anthropic prices its IPO at up to a $1.4 trillion valuation ahead of Thursday's Nasdaq debut, even as CISA adds six actively exploited flaws — spanning Cisco, Barracuda, Outlook and Chrome — to its must-patch list, LangChain raises $300 million at a $3 billion valuation, and SoftBank leads a $500 million round for German robotics maker Agile Robots. Product & Business: Home Depot's Q3 comparable sales turn positive for the first time in quarters as Eicher Motors calls its own best-ever quarter on record Royal Enfield and VECV sales, even as Vodafone Idea's loss widens on a one-off charge, India's October trade deficit hits a one-year high of $39.88 billion despite record exports, and Qualcomm tells staff its global layoff notifications begin this month. Stock Market: Nvidia's record $115.8 billion quarter and $150 billion buyback send its stock higher in after-hours trading even as its board rules out reinstating Jensen Huang, while GIFT Nifty signals a gap-down Wednesday open despite the good news, a day after Sensex and Nifty closed at a nine-month high and Bank Nifty hit a record.

entry.title: Edition 091 — 17 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Nvidia heads into tonight's first earnings call since Jensen Huang's resignation with interim CEO Colette Kress at the helm, as Anthropic closes out its IPO roadshow ahead of Wednesday's pricing and Thursday's Nasdaq debut, even as TrendForce forecasts another double-digit DRAM price jump for the fourth quarter, Sandisk's 8-for-1 stock split clears its final steps before Friday's split-adjusted trading, CISA's federal deadline for a four-flaw exploited-vulnerability batch has already passed, and AI-infrastructure orchestrator Edgevana signs over $700 million in Nvidia Blackwell deployment deals. Product & Business: Flipkart Group's FY26 revenue nears ₹1.5 lakh crore as its loss narrows to ₹8,468 crore and Trent's Q2 profit rises 23% to ₹464 crore the same week Noel Tata hands over as its chairman, GAIL's Q2 profit jumps to ₹4,650 crore as India's Q2 earnings season nears its close, Tata Sons heads toward a November 26 board meeting over Noel Tata's restructuring push and Shapoorji Pallonji's ₹25,000 crore exit proposal, Reliance moves to dissolve its UK Hamleys franchising unit, Lenny's Podcast guest Elena Verna argues AI companies need a rewritten growth playbook, and the US jobs report shows hiring beating expectations in October as layoffs keep falling even as Omnicom prepares to cut 15,000 roles. Stock Market: Wall Street's AI and chip stocks lead a sharp Monday selloff that puts the Nasdaq into correction territory as Nvidia's earnings and Anthropic's IPO pricing loom, GIFT Nifty signals a near-flat Tuesday open around 25,288 even as fresh data shows just 1,099 of 2,821 NSE stocks trading above their December 2025 closing levels despite this month's rally, and Home Depot, Target and Walmart's earnings this week line up to set Wall Street's holiday-season read.

entry.title: Edition 090 — 16 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Nvidia heads into Tuesday's first earnings call since Jensen Huang's resignation with interim CEO Colette Kress at the helm, as Anthropic's IPO roadshow enters its final two days with up to 20% of shares reserved for retail investors ahead of Wednesday's pricing and Thursday's Nasdaq debut, even as Google, Samsung, Warby Parker and Gentle Monster all open preorders for Gemini-powered smart eyewear, Microsoft's November Patch Tuesday fixes roughly 1,090 flaws including an actively exploited Outlook zero-day, CISA adds an actively exploited Cisco BroadWorks flaw to its federal must-patch list, and OpenAI strikes a deal with PayPal to let ChatGPT agents complete purchases. Product & Business: Oil India's Q2 profit rises 53% to ₹2,521 crore and Godrej Industries' more than doubles to ₹560 crore as India's Q2 earnings season winds down, Sun Pharma's profit holds near ₹1,990 crore on an 11.8% sales rise, Adani Enterprises' headline profit falls 55% even as its core business books record half-year EBITDA, and Shipping Corporation of India's profit more than triples to ₹577.8 crore, even as Indian startups raise just $162.9 million this week — down 32% — Coforge joins SpaceX's Grok enterprise network, and Stratechery's Ben Thompson argues the real risk in Jensen Huang's unraveling is governance, not national security. Stock Market: GIFT Nifty signals a positive Monday open near 25,242 as Brent crude eases toward $95 a barrel, even as Wall Street's own week of recovery sputtered to a halt on Friday with major indices closing mostly lower, Qualcomm's post-earnings guidance wobble still weighs on chip sentiment, and investors brace for Nvidia's Tuesday earnings and Anthropic's Wednesday IPO pricing to set the week's tone.

entry.title: Edition 089 — 15 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Nvidia still has no named successor to CEO Jensen Huang a month into open scrutiny of his conduct, as Anthropic launches Claude Meetings into open beta on Google Meet and China's public-comment window on export curbs covering 23 AI technologies closes today, even as Zyxel patches a zero-day that let attackers quietly compromise nearly 1,000 network switches across 48 countries, a second actively exploited Ivanti Connect Secure flaw's federal patch deadline passes, and a decade-old OpenSSH bug gets weaponized within two days of its fix. Product & Business: China blocks SoftBank's $5.4 billion bid for ABB's robotics division as Revolut confirms a $115 billion valuation after completing a secondary share sale, even as India's Q2 earnings season rolls on with Coal India's profit up 53% to ₹6,516 crore, Nykaa's more than tripling to ₹101 crore, PB Fintech's rising 43% to ₹192 crore, Bajaj Finance's climbing 29% to ₹6,367 crore, and Hero MotoCorp's up 41% to ₹1,861 crore. Stock Market: India's October retail inflation breaches the RBI's 6% ceiling for the first time in two years at 6.09%, as Brent crude logs its sharpest weekly drop since the pandemic to settle near $92, even as Bitcoin falls to a three-month low near $73,100 on hot US inflation data and rising Fed rate-hike bets.

entry.title: Edition 088 — 14 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Anthropic formally opens its $70–$78 IPO roadshow with Google and Nvidia among $26 billion of strategic buyers and reportedly locks in a separate $3.4 billion deal for its own gas generators, even as Google DeepMind ships both Gemini Robotics 2.5 and AlphaGenome 2 in the same week, China's draft export curbs covering 23 AI technologies near a November 15 comment deadline, and Microsoft's November Patch Tuesday fixes roughly 1,094 flaws including an actively exploited Outlook zero-day. Product & Business: Manappuram Finance's Q2 profit more than triples to ₹701 crore and Hitachi Energy India's surges 63.5% on an order-inflow boom, as SoftBank's Meesho-backing vehicle moves to sell a ₹1,174 crore stake and Bodhi Tree Systems buys a majority stake in Adyar Ananda Bhavan for $180 million, even as Lenskart's profit more than doubles to ₹232 crore, Crystal Crop Protection files for a ₹450.9 crore IPO, NATCO Pharma posts a ₹203 crore Q2 profit, and product veteran Marty Cagan argues the feature-roadmap era is over. Stock Market: Sensex and Nifty snap a three-day winning streak as rising crude and a hotter-than-expected October inflation print drag Dalal Street lower on Friday, even as Wall Street closes out its best week since August despite Nvidia sliding roughly 13% off its November 6 peak, and a Q2-earnings-driven session sends Hitachi Energy up over 10% and MSTC to a 20% upper circuit while Raksan Transformers drops 12.75%.

entry.title: Edition 087 — 13 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Nvidia ousts Jensen Huang as CEO after his affair admission and a Chinese-intelligence probe, naming CFO Colette Kress interim chief, even as Anthropic locks in a November 18 IPO pricing date and November 19 Nasdaq debut, OpenAI secures $11 billion of a trimmed $20 billion funding round, a threat actor is found chaining all three Ivanti Connect Secure zero-days since October, and Samsung and SK Hynix reportedly seek to raise iPhone memory prices by as much as 100%. Product & Business: Blackstone agrees to invest ₹5,000 crore for a roughly 16% stake in IIFL Finance as India's GST collections hit their second-highest month ever at ₹2.31 lakh crore, even as Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal defends his ₹85,000 Temple wearable against doctors calling it a health scam, Canva cuts 1,271 roles in what its CEO calls the company's "hardest year yet," Stratechery's Ben Thompson argues Nvidia's governance — not China optics — was always the real risk in Jensen Huang's fall, and India Inc's Q2 earnings season crosses two-thirds complete with median profit growth near 24%. Stock Market: Sensex and Nifty eke out a marginally higher close in a volatile Thursday session as realty surges and auto lags, even as Wall Street slides after Nvidia sinks 4.34% on Jensen Huang's abrupt ouster and the 10-year Treasury yield climbs to 5.10%, and Marvell's $115 billion all-stock bid for Lumentum — the biggest tech deal of the year — hands Lumentum holders a 23.9% premium.

entry.title: Edition 086 — 12 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: CoreWeave's Q3 revenue surges 168% and sends Wall Street back into the AI trade, even as Anthropic's IPO book runs several times oversubscribed and Google locks in an option on $10 billion of its stock, OpenAI opens a "Businesses in ChatGPT" hub with sponsored AI sales agents, Jensen Huang lets a congressional-briefing deadline pass without public comment, and Team Group's own numbers show the DDR5 memory shortage still hasn't peaked. Product & Business: Noel Tata steps down from six Tata Group boards on his 70th birthday while holding his ground at Tata Sons, even as Jio Platforms posts its first results as a standalone-listed company, Ather Energy crosses 300,000 scooters sold for the year, Clinics On Cloud and Peppermint Robotics lead a $290 million week for Indian startup funding, Myntra and Flipkart's combined festive fashion share slides to 76.8% from 89%, and UPI crosses ₹1 lakh crore in daily transaction value for the first time. Stock Market: Sensex and Nifty rally to their highest close since February on a PSU-bank and auto-led surge, even as Wall Street logs its best session in weeks after CoreWeave's earnings beat revives the AI trade, and M&M, IndiGo and Trent lead Indian gainers while Adani Ports, ICICI Bank and Tech Mahindra lag.

entry.title: Edition 085 — 11 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Anthropic locks in a $70–$78 IPO price range valuing it at up to $1.4 trillion ahead of a November 19 Nasdaq debut, even as Jensen Huang faces a November 11 deadline to even propose an alternate date for a congressional briefing over his alleged Chinese-intelligence contact, Microsoft winds down its 2023 Oracle AI-cloud-rental deal, OpenAI hires the security researchers who once breached it to red-team its own systems, and Qualcomm's soft guidance overshadows an 89% jump in its automotive revenue. Product & Business: PhysicsWallah's headcount shrinks as it credits AI efficiencies for part of the cut, even as MakeMyTrip's India unit reportedly clears SEBI's hurdle for an IPO and buys into ride-pooling startup Quick Ride, EloElo Group raises $80 million to take its microdrama app global, JSW Steel's profit more than triples while Rentomojo's falls 62% despite a 53% revenue jump, and India Inc's Q2 earnings season nears its finish with median profit growth near 24%. Stock Market: Indian markets reopen from the Diwali-Balipratipada break with GIFT Nifty signaling a roughly 300-point gap-up as crude cools and FIIs revive buying, even as Wall Street closes lower for a second day on a hotter-than-expected October inflation print and foreign funds pile a near-record $1.6 billion into Indian equities in a single day as the global AI trade falters.

entry.title: Edition 084 — 10 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Anthropic emails bankers IPO pricing figures it retracts hours later as inaccurate, even as a November 12 deadline cuts off Cursor's access to OpenAI's models, Jensen Huang faces a November 11 deadline to even schedule a congressional briefing over an alleged Chinese-intelligence contact, OpenAI pledges to cover its own data centers' electricity costs after its side lost nearly every November 3 ballot measure, and Beijing's draft AI export curbs near a November 15 comment deadline. Product & Business: Titan's net profit more than doubles to ₹2,393 crore on a one-off gain as Noel N. Tata prepares to retire as its Vice Chairman, even as Bank of Baroda posts a record ₹6,532 crore quarterly profit and Adani Ports raises its full-year guidance while Adani Enterprises' headline profit falls 55% on the same quarter's 75% revenue surge, while Mahindra & Mahindra, MapmyIndia and Saregama all post double-digit profit growth and Bengaluru cleantech startup altM raises a $10.3 million Series A. Stock Market: NSE and BSE close for Diwali-Balipratipada a day after Sensex and Nifty inch to an eight-month high on muted 0.13% and 0.23% gains, even as Wall Street logs its best session since April on tumbling crude and a chip-stock rebound, foreign investors keep adding to Indian government bonds as the rupee strengthens, and IREDA extends its winning streak to a seventh session.

entry.title: Edition 083 — 9 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Anthropic's own prospective IPO investors reportedly push its valuation talk down toward $1 trillion from an earlier $2 trillion, even as AI-inference startup fal doubles its own valuation to $16 billion in a $1.3 billion round, OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic jointly back a shared opt-out token for publishers against AI training, and a federal November 13 deadline looms over an already-exploited, two-bug Ivanti zero-day chain. Product & Business: Bharti Airtel's Q2 profit rises 31% to ₹8,888 crore even as it misses Street estimates and Nykaa's profit triples to ₹101 crore, even as Tata Trusts' Darius Khambata quits rather than seek reappointment, calling September's board vote reappointing N. Chandrasekaran "a day that will live in infamy," while India's startup funding rebounds to $255 million this week on jewellery brand GIVA's ₹975 crore round and Shiprocket swings to its first quarterly profit. Stock Market: Samvat 2083 opens in the red on a rare Sunday Muhurat session, snapping Sensex and Nifty's eight-year winning streak, even as the outgoing Samvat 2082 closes as benchmarks' worst year in 15 years and brokerages split on how far a recovery can run.

entry.title: Edition 082 — 8 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Independent evaluator METR finds Anthropic’s AI-assisted research running roughly 2x faster than a year ago and says Anthropic redacted most of its supporting evidence, even as the company’s first Wall Street stock analyst declines to rate it ahead of its IPO roadshow and Blackstone warns its post-IPO credit rating could land below investment grade. Product & Business: India’s startup funding slumps to its weakest month in years at just $678 million in October with no single round crossing $100 million, even as LG Electronics India’s profit climbs 25.65% to ₹489 crore and the National Stock Exchange’s own Q2 profit rises 23% to ₹2,578 crore on the same trading boom reshaping Dalal Street. Stock Market: NSE and BSE hold a rare Sunday Muhurat trading session marking the start of Samvat 2083, a tradition BSE has observed since 1957 and NSE since 1992, even as the outgoing Samvat 2082 closes with the Nifty and Sensex both down roughly 7-8% despite Friday’s seven-session Dhanteras rally.

entry.title: Edition 081 — 7 November 2026
entry.summary: AI & Tech: Anthropic’s amended S-1/A warns Claude may be nearing a self-improvement threshold even as its own public-filing clock sets November 16 as the earliest possible Nasdaq trading day, while chip stocks claw back Thursday’s rout with AMD leading a Friday rebound and an AI-driven memory shortage leaves Western Digital sold out of hard-drive capacity through 2026. Product & Business: Stratechery’s Ben Thompson frames Apple’s earnings-day memory-cost warning as “The Hardware Company Regression,” even as India’s Q2 FY27 earnings season crosses its halfway mark with median profit growth near 21% and Cholamandalam Investment and Finance’s profit jumps 41% to ₹1,630 crore alongside a ₹5,000 crore fundraise. Stock Market: Sensex and Nifty extend their rally to a seventh straight session as the Nifty reclaims 25,000 for the first time since February on Dhanteras, even as Wall Street’s own Friday rebound claws back only part of Thursday’s correction-triggering rout, with a rare Sunday Muhurat trading session still to come.

entry.title: Edition 080 — 6 November 2026
